title: Pseudo-Palindromic Paths in a Binary Tree
spaceBreakdown:
- int mask (passed by value): O(1)
- int& count: O(1)
- recursion call-stack depth: O(h), worst case O(n) for skewed tree, O(log n) for balanced
- not counted: input tree, returned int
approach: A sequence can be rearranged into a palindrome iff at most one digit has an odd frequency. Since node values are 1-9, we track each digit's parity with a 9-bit integer mask, toggling bit `v` when we visit a node with value `v`. We DFS from root to leaves; at each leaf we check `mask & (mask-1) == 0` (at most one bit set). This visits every node once, giving O(n) time and O(h) recursion depth.
hints: A sequence can be rearranged into a palindrome only under what condition on how many of its elements appear an odd number of times? Node values here are restricted to 1 through 9.

Use DFS carrying a 9-bit mask where bit `v` tracks the parity of digit `v`; toggle it at each node. At a leaf, the path is pseudo-palindromic when `mask & (mask-1) == 0`. Example: path [2,3,3] yields mask = `100` (only bit 2 set), so it counts.

```
dfs(node, mask):
    if node is null: return
    mask = mask XOR (1 << node.val)
    if node is leaf:
        if (mask AND (mask - 1)) == 0:
            count = count + 1
    else:
        dfs(node.left, mask)
        dfs(node.right, mask)
```

**Single node** - The tree has exactly one node with no children.
`Input: root = [9]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: incrementing count only inside recursive child calls with no explicit leaf check → returns 0

**All same values, odd path length** - Every node on the path has the same digit, appearing an odd number of times.
`Input: root = [1,1,null,1]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: checking `mask == 0` (all even) instead of `mask & (mask-1) == 0` → returns 0

**All distinct values** - A path where every digit appears exactly once.
`Input: root = [1,2,null,3]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: checking `mask != 0` (any odd frequency) instead of at most one bit set → returns 1

**Right-skewed tree** - The tree is a linked list going only through right children.
`Input: root = [1,null,2,null,1]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: checking only `!node->left` for leaf detection (ignoring right child) → returns 0

followUps.q: What if node values could be 0-9 instead of 1-9?
followUps.a: The mask simply grows to 10 bits; `1 << node->val` still fits in a 32-bit int and `mask & (mask-1) == 0` works unchanged. Time and space complexity stay O(n) and O(h).

followUps.q: What if we must count pseudo-palindromic paths between any two nodes, not just root-to-leaf?
followUps.a: This becomes a path-pair counting problem: for each node as the LCA, combine parity masks from different subtrees and count pairs whose XOR has at most one bit set. Time becomes O(n · 10) with O(h) stack space, using subtree mask frequency arrays.

followUps.q: What if the tree has 10^7 nodes, too deep for recursion?
followUps.a: Convert the DFS to an explicit stack-based iteration storing (node, mask) pairs. Time stays O(n); space becomes O(h) for the explicit stack instead of the call stack, avoiding stack overflow on skewed trees.
